articles.name: Principles relating to processing of personal data
articles.description: Lawfulness, fairness, transparency; purpose limitation; data minimisation; accuracy; storage limitation; integrity and confidentiality (5(1)(f)); accountability (5(2)).

articles.name: Lawfulness of processing
articles.description: A valid legal basis (consent, contract, legal obligation, vital interests, public task, legitimate interests) is required.

articles.name: Responsibility of the controller
articles.description: Implement appropriate technical and organisational measures and be able to demonstrate compliance (accountability).

articles.name: Data protection by design and by default
articles.description: Embed data protection into processing and default to the minimum necessary data.

Processor
articles.description: Use only processors providing sufficient guarantees; govern processing by a written contract with required terms, including audits (28(3)(h)).

articles.name: Processing under the authority of the controller or processor
Security of processing
articles.description: Appropriate technical and organisational measures: pseudonymisation/encryption (32(1)(a)); confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience (32(1)(b)); restore availability (32(1)(c)); testing (32(1)(d)).

articles.name: Notification of a personal data breach to the supervisory authority
articles.description: Notify the competent supervisory authority without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours of becoming aware. Maintain a breach register (33(5)).

articles.name: Communication of a personal data breach to the data subject
articles.description: Communicate to affected individuals without undue delay when the breach is likely to result in a high risk to their rights and freedoms.

articles.name: Data protection impact assessment
articles.description: Assess high-risk processing before it begins.
